sections.section_name: Section B (Short Answer Questions - 3 Marks Each)

questions.question_text: Contrast incandescent bulbs and LEDs regarding energy efficiency and heat generation.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Incandescent bulbs generate light by heating a filament to high temperatures, wasting significant energy as heat. LEDs convert electrical energy directly into light with minimal heat waste.

questions.question_text: Describe the practical activity with aim: 'To construct a simple functional switch using safety pins and drawing pins.'. Outline key steps and conclusion.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Steps: Insert one drawing pin through the ring end of a safety pin and press into cardboard., Fix the second drawing pin on cardboard such that the free end of the safety pin can touch it., Connect wires from the drawing pins to complete a circuit with a cell and bulb., Rotate the safety pin to touch (ON) or leave a gap (OFF).
Conclusion: A switch regulates current flow by closing or opening the electrical circuit gap.

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer & Case Study - 5 Marks Each)

questions.question_text: Explain how an LED works, detail lead identification rules, and draw schematic circuit diagrams for functional (forward-biased) and non-functional (reverse-biased) LED circuits.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: An LED is a polar semiconductor light source. Lead identification: Longer lead = Positive (+) Anode; Shorter lead = Negative (-) Cathode. Forward-Biased Circuit: Longer lead connected to cell positive terminal, shorter lead to switch and cell negative terminal; LED glows bright. Reverse-Biased Circuit: Longer lead connected to cell negative terminal; current is blocked and LED remains dark.

questions.question_text:
Case Scenario: An electrician uses rubber gloves and plastic-handled pliers while repairing household electrical switches.
Question: Why are rubber and plastic used on electrical repair tools?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Rubber and plastic are electrical insulators (poor conductors) that prevent electric current from flowing through the tools into the human body, preventing electric shocks.

questions.question_text: Why must electric cells in a multi-cell torch be connected positive-terminal-to-negative-terminal?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Series connection (+ to -) combines the individual voltage potentials of the cells, driving sufficient electromotive force through the filament to produce bright light. Connecting like terminals (+ to +) cancels potential.
